name: SOFA
listed_description: SOFA is an open-source framework targeting at real-time simulation, with an emphasis on medical simulation.
reason: No numeric comparison against ODE, Bullet or any other engine in reachable sources. The README (raw.githubusercontent.com) says only 'interactive physics simulation based on the Finite Element Method' and lists comparison of algorithms inside SOFA as a feature, with no numbers; the repo page and the sofa-framework organisation page show a PerformanceRegression plugin (tracks SOFA's own regressions, not other engines) and nothing else on speed. sofa-framework.org and the SOFA papers were not reachable and the WebSearch budget (10 queries) was used up on other projects, so a paper or blog comparison may exist.

name: TensorComprehensions
listed_description: A fully-functional C++ library to automatically synthesize high-performance machine learning kernels.
reason: No baseline comparison with numbers in reachable sources. The README gives only absolute autotuning timings (best/median/worst 226/4238/7345 us in generation 0, 220/221/233 us in generation 1, kernel runs of 239 us, 56 us and 210 us) and a claim of '80%+ of peak shared memory bandwidth', with no named baseline. docs/source/performance.rst says TC 'will not beat libraries such as CUBLAS and CUDNN except in very specific corner cases' and defers to its paper (arXiv 1802.04730) for those cases. tc/benchmarks/*.cc holds TC-vs-ATen-vs-Caffe2 test harnesses for P100 and V100 (for example batchmatmul.cc, with stored autotuned options), but no timings are stored in the repo. The paper and the Facebook announcement post (arxiv.org, ar5iv.org, research.facebook.com) were EGRESS_BLOCKED and the WebSearch budget was exhausted; a retier in an environment that can open arXiv 1802.04730 could reach tier B. The repo was archived on 2023-04-28 (last commit 2023-04-28), license Apache-2.0, 1.8k stars.
